Spicule Routine

Show how your skin changed after using spicule serum every night.

1

Spicule care

What is spicule care?

  • It's a serum with spicules in it. Tiny natural spikes, too small to see.
  • When you pat it in, they open tiny pathways in your skin. That's the tingle.
  • It's the spicules doing it, not an ingredient, so people call it physical care.
  • Your skin starts making its own collagen, and whatever you put on next gets in easier.

What it does

  • Smoother texture. Bumps and rough spots even out.
  • Smaller-looking pores, and a glow you can see by morning.
  • Whatever you put on next sinks in better. Try it with azelaic acid or peptides.
2

How to shoot it

The lines are examples. Change them so they sound like you.
1

Old clips

Cut together four or five old clips of your skin at its worst. Big pores, blackheads, bumps, rough texture. Keep the same angle in every clip, and get close.

On screenpov: you've tried everything and your pores still look like this
Say"this was my skin for the longest time. acids, masks, I'd tried pretty much everything"
2

Me now

Your skin now, from that same angle. Clear glass skin, so you can see the difference right away. Say how long you've been using it.

On screenand this is me now:
Say"then I started spicule care every night. my texture's never been this smooth"
3

What I used

Squeeze it onto your face and pat it in on camera. Don't say its name. Just call it spicule serum.

On screentingle = it's working
Say"it's a spicule serum. the tingle means it's working, and whatever I put on after just sinks in"
3

Do's and don'ts

Do

  • No filter on any clip
  • Say spicule serum out loud at least once
  • Keep the bottle on screen long enough to read the label

Don't

  • Say the brand or product name out loud
  • Say needles or microneedling
  • Say cured or healed
  • Name other brands
  • Do an unboxing
